title: Data Detective
description: Solve mysteries with data! Dot the fox detective hands you case files: sort and group a table until the answer pops out, pick the chart that answers the question, build bars to match a table, judge whether a claim is supported, not supported or too early to tell, predict the next bar, clean up messy lists (typos, repeats and impossible numbers) and turn counts into percent to compare fairly. The Show-me rule: you can only pin a claim when the view on screen supports it, and you prove it by tapping the evidence. Explorer and Pro cases, stars for sharp detective work, no typing anywhere.
notes: Built on the Oomba Kit 1.1.2 (pinned kit tag plus the art-props, dress and style-bold packs; Would You Rather pattern): a kit stage (forest, props, Dot = kit fox with glasses and an inline SVG trench coat on her DOM portrait) behind DOM case cards appended to Oomba.ui.root(); the kit's title (audit-visible Play), dialogs (case files and learn cards with Dot's portrait), quiz card (the Case-closed concept check in lesson mode), results (Oomba.ui.win), pause (P / Esc / HUD button, bound by the game since it does not use Oomba.game) and settings (title corner and the Quest Card gear). Levels are data: window.DataDetectiveLevels (CHAPTERS, LEVELS, NAMES, VERDICTS, allStrings) and a pure engine window.DataDetectiveEngine (newCase(level, seed) -> state; act(level, state, action) for sort / group / view / bar / set / slider / pct / fix / merge / remove / claim / show / hint / skip; evidence(); stars(); series(); visibleRows()) in the first classic script, vm-loadable, no DOM. Every case: case file dialog, a data view (DOM table with sort-by-header buttons and data-fit-dense rows, grouped counts, bar chart or pictograph as role=img bars with printed values, never canvas), tools (Group by, Table / Bars / Pictures, +/- steppers, a prediction slider, a row panel with Fix to / Merge / Remove / Keep, a percent toggle), Dot's panel (hints and what the data actually shows after a wrong claim) and the claim card. Show-me rule: the claim card opens only when the evidence view on screen supports it (engine.evidence), and a right claim is accepted once the player taps the evidence rows or bars (level.proof). Stars: 1 solved, 2 well made (edits within par, no wrong claim, no good row removed), 3 no tier-3 hint; Skip appears after two failed claims (0 stars, unlocks the next case). Chapters (quest code index): 1 sort (6), 2 chart (5), 3 claims (6), 4 cleanup (6), 5 models (5), 6 fair (4), 7 my-data (tally mode); Explorer plays 1-3 and 7, Pro plays 4-7 with 1 as review (Explorer stars show silver for Pro). Lesson mode = BRB.params ({chapter, band, mode, level, lock}, read as (window.BRB && BRB.params) || {}) or a 4-digit quest code C B M L typed on the in-game keypad (digits in groups with spaces, hidden in live frames; params win over codes): skips the chapter map, shows 'Class quest: <chapter> · <band>', enables the Case-closed card (3-tile check + a confidence face) and with lock=1 hides the map and the band toggle; at chapter end the results card says the work is saved. Progress: after every solved or skipped case BRB.score.submit(starsInChapter, '<done>/<total> cases, <stars> stars[, <ok>/<n> checks]'), BRB.gameOver({won: true, score}) at chapter end, BRB.progress({game: 'dd', ...}) when the SDK has it. Modes: play, tally (My Data), projector (bigger text, nothing saved). Saves in BRB.storage 'data-detective-v1' (band, stars per level, learn cards seen, pairs). Words: English is the key (window.DataDetectiveT), other languages are reviewed data packs under /vendor/data/data-detective/<PACK_VER>/<lang>.js read from window.CsqPacks (scripts/cs-quest-i18n.mjs). Test hooks: __brbTest.start({chapter, band, mode, level, seed, lesson, lock}), step, skipAnimations, cover, state, act, tap, claim, hint, skip, solve, closeDialog, params, code, questCard, keypad, map, levels; deterministic layouts from seed.
